title: Number of Islands
kidExplanation: A map of water and land squares. Land sticks to up/down/left/right neighbors. How many separate islands?
plainProblem: LeetCode 200: Number of Islands. Restate the official prompt in your own words, list inputs and outputs, then solve a tiny example by hand before coding.

thinkingSteps.title: Brute force idea
thinkingSteps.body: For Number of Islands, first describe a slow but correct approach (often nested loops or rescanning).

thinkingSteps.title: Why it is slow
thinkingSteps.body: Count the loops. If work looks like n×n, say so. Google interviewers want that honesty.

thinkingSteps.title: Aha insight
thinkingSteps.body: The problem is to count the number of islands in a 2D grid where '1' represents land and '0' represents water. We can solve this problem using Depth-First Search (DFS) algorithm. For each cell that contains '1', we perform DFS to explore all adjacent land cells and mark them as visited by changing their value to '0'. This way, we count each connected component of '1's as a separate island.
